title: Pachangaworld.
content: "*Pachanga* is an informal word to say ‘party’ and it’s very popular among all Mexican Spanish speakers. Even though it’s not a rule of thumb, ‘pachanga’ implies a lively party with music, dancing, and some drinking. On top of being used in Mexico, ‘pachanga’ is also popular in some Latin American countries." Last night I had a dream about a party at a large sprawling venue that lives in perpetual night. I think this was heavily influenced by the seemingly universal Mexican-American experience of being a child forced to attend parties in rented spaces that last til midnight or later for every quasi-religious holiday, 15-year-old girls' birthday, wedding, baptism, and any other excuse that adults in a self isolated ethnic enclave make to drink and dance. The influence was obvious to me because my mother was in the dream at the age she was when I was a kid, but I seemed to be my current age. That, and the blasting bassy Spanish music that likely contributed to my very real tinnitus. The venue was like every single Elks Lodge or Shriner's Hall or any of the litany of fraternal orders that have rentable spaces for parties, a main hall, a kitchen, and small side hallways with bathrooms and glass cases filled with types of rewards these organizations award themselves, the hallways and kitchen in particular gave the dream venue that 'liminal space' feeling of being in a transitory area with endless doors, a place where you aren't really supposed to be opening random doors, but when you're a bored and unsupervised kid, who is going to stop you? Stepping outside the venue seemed to be folded into the larger reality I call 'Resortworld', the beachside hotel with sand dunes so high they reach the upper floors of the hotel and let visitors walk down them to beach from their hotel room windows, tucked next the perpetual fair or carnival complete with suspiciously maintained rides, rigged games and vaguely Latino food vendors. This reality feels nestled into a larger reality I call 'Parkworld', a sprawling outdoor park complete with trees, gravel paths, muddy desire trails cut by years of human feet insisting on shortcuts, wild animals, rocky hills, streams and rivers and other bodies of water and boggy areas, and small rentable cabins that are most assuredly haunted. I think this is influenced by the second most likely place for a Mexican party, a park. I didn't leave the venue, but I knew it was tucked into all these various levels of self-contained reality in that way someone simply knows things to be true in a dream, possibly contextually informed by the unending night surrounding the party.
